answer: Shared-secret fingerprint challenge.** Each agent gets a unique numeric seed; a central willow ledger stores only a compressed hash of each seed’s derived outputs. On any action, the agent must answer a fresh challenge derived from its seed and a public prism of rotating salts, so replies never repeat. Duplicate identities would need to reproduce the same seed’s output chain, revealing collision; distinct seeds cost one walnut-priced registration each, making mass sybils linearly expensive while forcing every clone to expose itself through mismatched challenge answers.
